name: Layout
intent: Page-level spacing and structure: layout pattern classes and layout tokens. Agents use these for content edge padding and vertical rhythm between sections — not per-component padding or raw px.
usage: Spacing follows a 4px grid (`--ref-space-200` = 4px; named `--space-*` matches the same ladder). Wrap the scrollable page body in `.layout-content` (or an equivalent layout class from this file). Its `padding` uses `--layout-margin-md` (24px) for content edge inset. Its `gap` uses `--layout-gutter-lg` (24px) for space between stacked children, such as Section blocks. When Sections stack inside a layout rather than directly in the page body, such as a side column of a `.layout-split`, wrap that column in `.layout-stack`: the same 24px gap between blocks, with no edge padding and no scrolling of its own. Section only spaces header to body inside itself (`--space-medium`, 16px); the page supplies side padding via the layout class. A page header is the exception: the bar is the top of the page, so it pulls up through that top inset and sits flush against the frame's bar, with its own block padding standing in for the inset. The patterns that hold a PageHeader (AppShell, RecordPage) already do that; screens do not. See contracts/layout.json for the full contract. The layout classes break twice, at 1024px and 640px, and they answer to the box they are in as well as to the window: a frame can be a phone-width box inside a wide window, and there the window says nothing about the room a layout has. .layout-split and the fixed metrics grids drop to one column at the mobile break.
useWhen: Setting page or content-area edge padding and vertical rhythm between sections.
Stacking Sections or cards in a column inside another layout, such as the main or side column of `.layout-split`: use `.layout-stack`.
doNot: Do not add outer padding or margin to Section for page inset or between-section gap. Use `.layout-content` (or the matching layout class).
Do not put an inline `gap` or a flex wrapper around a column of Sections. Use `.layout-stack`; use `.layout-content` only for the page body, since it adds page padding.
Do not invent per-page grids, PageContent wrappers, or layout cousins.
Do not leave the page's top inset above a page header, and do not cancel it in the screen. The pattern holding the PageHeader owns that.

Do not use raw px, magic numbers, or `--ref-space-*` / `--ui-*` primitives in components. Use layout tokens (`--layout-margin-*`, `--layout-gutter-*`) via layout classes, or semantic `--space-*` inside components.
a11y: Layout classes are structural only; they do not replace landmarks or headings.
